To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The dimension of the attractor of human gait is a good estimate of the degrees of freedom that are actively controlled in walking.
the complexity of walking is related to the number of degrees of freedom that have to be controlled and that walking at slower speeds becomes more complex.

the attractor structure of the state space of joint angle trajectories of normal human walking is a low-dimensional torus with a fractal dimension between 1.7 and 2.2, and that the dimension of the attractor is influenced by the walking speed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of complex movement trajectories.
the application of methods from non-linear dynamics in the analysis of human movement.
the application of methods from nonlinear dynamics to gait analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the complexity of the human gait is influenced by the walking speed, but that the complexity is not directly proportional to the walking speed, and that the walking speed is not directly proportional.
the complexity of human walking increases with decreasing walking speed.
the dimension of movement trajectory increases with decreasing speed, which indicates a greater number of degrees of freedom to be controlled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the state-space analysis of joint-angle kinematics is a powerful tool to analyze the dynamics of human locomotion.
human walking can be described in terms of an attractor in state-space.
the complexity of the attractor in the state-space is an indicator of the amount of control required by the central nervous system to perform the movement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now use tools from nonlinear dynamics to study human locomotion and other movement tasks in more detail.
the dimension of movement is an interesting measure of the control of movement and may be used to quantify movement control in patients.
the state-space analysis of kinematic data is an appropriate tool for studying the dynamics of human locomotion and for gaining insight into the underlying mechanisms of motor control.
